headline: DepEd Proposes Joint School Safety Task Force After Banga Shooting
seoTitle: DepEd Proposes Joint School Safety Task Force After Banga Shooting | FMB News
seoDescription: Education Secretary Sonny Angara has proposed a joint DepEd-DILG-PNP school safety task force for site-specific security audits after the fatal Banga National High School shooting.
deck: Education Secretary Sonny Angara has proposed a joint DepEd-DILG-PNP task force to conduct site-specific security audits in public schools nationwide. The proposal follows the September 18 Banga National High School shooting and is not yet a completed nationwide rollout.
author: FMB News Desk

relatedReports.headline: Three Students Dead, Eight Injured in Banga National High School Shooting

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Education Secretary Sonny Angara on Saturday proposed creating a Joint School Safety Task Force with the Department of the Interior and Local Government and the Philippine National Police to conduct site-specific security audits in public schools nationwide after the fatal shooting at Banga National High School in South Cotabato.

DepEd's official social-media account announced the proposal on September 19. Independent reports by NewsWatch Plus, GMA News and Daily Tribune separately reported Angara's visit to Banga and the department's planned security response.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The proposed task force would assess school entry controls, threat reporting, emergency response and coordination with local police to identify security gaps and recommend interventions. Angara also said DepEd has purchased additional metal detectors, although he did not give a distribution timetable, and that the department is hiring more School Counselor Associates as part of its mental-health response.

DepEd said it has deployed psychological first-aid teams in Banga and is reviewing existing campus-safety guidelines. The department has also asked barangay officials and tanods to supplement police patrols, particularly around schools without security guards.

sections.heading: What is not yet settled
paragraphs: The Joint School Safety Task Force is a proposal. FMB News is not reporting it as an already constituted body or as proof that nationwide security audits have begun. Details including formal authority, implementation timetable, staffing, funding and the scope of any mandatory security changes remain to be announced.

Authorities are separately investigating the Banga shooting. Statements by officials linking the suspected shooter's online activity to the attack remain investigative claims rather than a conclusively established motive. Police are examining the student's devices and other evidence.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The September 18 attack at Banga National High School killed two students and the suspected student gunman and injured other students. It followed other fatal school shootings in Tacloban and Zamboanga in recent months, increasing pressure on education and law-enforcement agencies to reassess campus security.

This report is a continuation of FMB News' September 18 account of the Banga shooting. It focuses on the independently newsworthy policy response announced after that initial report rather than republishing the incident itself.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A nationwide, site-specific audit could shift school-security policy from uniform guidance toward risk assessments tailored to individual campuses. Its effectiveness will depend on whether the proposal becomes an operational program, whether identified vulnerabilities receive funding, and whether security measures are balanced with students' access, privacy and well-being.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for a formal DepEd, DILG or PNP order establishing the task force; the audit methodology and timetable; rules governing metal detectors, guards and police coordination; funding commitments; and the PNP's final investigative findings in the Banga case. Claims about motive or online influence should remain provisional until investigators establish supporting evidence.

verificationNotes: DepEd's official social-media account announced that Secretary Sonny Angara proposed a Joint School Safety Task Force with DILG and PNP for site-specific security audits in public schools nationwide and linked to a DepEd release.

NewsWatch Plus independently reported the task-force proposal at 3:15 p.m. on September 19 and described its intended audit areas: entry controls, threat reporting, emergency response and local-police coordination.

GMA News independently reported Angara's statements in South Cotabato that DepEd plans enhanced safety measures, has purchased additional metal detectors without announcing a distribution date, and is hiring more School Counselor Associates.

Daily Tribune independently reported Angara's Banga visit, DepEd's psychological-first-aid deployment, requested barangay patrol support, comprehensive review of campus-safety guidelines, and the proposed joint task force.
The article distinguishes the task-force proposal from an established or operational nationwide program and does not state that audits have begun.
Claims about online influence on the suspected shooter are identified as investigative claims, not established causation.

The hero image is the same rights-cleared contextual photograph used in FMB News' earliest Banga report. Wikimedia Commons identifies Tdorante10 as creator and licenses the work CC BY-SA 4.0. The caption clearly states that it is a January 2023 file photograph.
